stem: Before releasing the medication, a Dayvigo prescription has two refills used and is three months old. The next refill is requested. Which federal limits should be checked together?

choices.text: Check only whether five refills have been completed after documenting whether 21 CFR 1306.22 had no separate six-month limit.
Check only whether six months have elapsed.
Check both the five-refill maximum and six-month issue-date window; neither is yet exhausted on these facts.
Require renewal now because two prior refills exhaust the limit.
Use a one-year window because Dayvigo is prescribed for sleep.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Check both the five-refill maximum and six-month issue-date window; neither is yet exhausted on these facts.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Check only whether five refills have been completed.' would require that 21 CFR 1306.22 had no separate six-month limit. The decisive cue appears in 'Before releasing the medication, a Dayvigo prescription has two refills used and is three months old. The next refill is requested. Which federal limits should be checked together?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Check only whether five refills have been completed.' would apply only if 21 CFR 1306.22 had no separate six-month limit; 'Before releasing the medication, a Dayvigo prescription has two refills used and is three months old. The next refill is requested. Which federal limits should be checked together?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Check only whether six months have elapsed.' would apply only if the rule imposed no numerical maximum; 'Before releasing the medication, a Dayvigo prescription has two refills used and is three months old. The next refill is requested. Which federal limits should be checked together?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Check both the five-refill maximum and six-month issue-date window; neither is yet exhausted on these facts.': supported by schedule iii-iv refills.
choice_analysis.D: 'Require renewal now because two prior refills exhaust the limit.' would apply only if the federal cap were two refills; 'Before releasing the medication, a Dayvigo prescription has two refills used and is three months old. The next refill is requested. Which federal limits should be checked together?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Use a one-year window because Dayvigo is prescribed for sleep.' would apply only if indication altered the Schedule IV refill period; 'Before releasing the medication, a Dayvigo prescription has two refills used and is three months old. The next refill is requested. Which federal limits should be checked together?' states otherwise.

related_facts: lemborexant (Dayvigo) is used for treatment of insomnia with sleep-onset or sleep-maintenance difficulty; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
